newsitem.title: USA: US tax bill has net cut $94 bln over five years.
newsitem.headline: US tax bill has net cut $94 bln over five years.

text.p: U.S. tax legislation agreed to by congressional leaders and the White House would amount to a net $94 billion tax cut over five years, a senior congressional aide said Tuesday.
Revenue increases would amount to about $55.5 billion over five years, including $5.2 billion from a cigarette tax increase, the aide said.

Capital gains tax cut provisions were estimated to raise about $20 million over five years on expectations for an initial stepped-up selling of assets, and therefore more taxes paid on profits, by investors taking advantage of lower rates.
Over 10 years the capital gains tax cuts would cost $20.1 billion, the aide said.
The tax bill did not include a capital gains tax cut for corporations, a provision that was dropped in the earlier unified House-Senate Republican tax plan.
The tobacco tax increase of 10 cents a pack starting in 2000 and 15 cents a pack in 2002 will be attached to the spending bill, not the tax bil.
The $500 per-child tax credit was expected to cost about $85 billion over five years and the higher education tax incentives $40 billion, the aide said.

The airline tax package would raise about $33 billion over five years. Provisions to expand Individual Retirement Accounts were expected to cost $1.8 billion over five years and $20.2 billion over 10 years.
